Modern Electrical Panel Upgrades for Inglewood Homes and Businesses

One of the most common electrical projects Shaffer Construction completes in Inglewood is electrical panel upgrades. Many homes and commercial buildings in the area were built during the 1960s through 1980s and still rely on outdated electrical panels that pose serious safety risks and cannot handle modern electrical loads. Panels manufactured by companies like Zinsco, Federal Pacific, Pushmatic, and Challenger are known to fail inspections and have been linked to electrical fires due to faulty circuit breakers that do not trip properly when overloaded.

Modern electrical systems require significantly more capacity than systems installed just a few decades ago. While older homes typically had 60-amp or 100-amp service panels, today's homes benefit from 200-amp or even 400-amp panels to accommodate the increased electrical demand from central air conditioning, multiple large appliances, home offices with extensive electronics, and most importantly, electric vehicle charging equipment. According to electrical contractors throughout Los Angeles, upgrading to a higher-capacity panel can increase property values by 2-5% while also improving safety and preventing frequent circuit breaker trips.

The National Fire Protection Association publishes the National Electrical Code, which is updated every three years. The NEC 2023 edition, now being adopted throughout California, includes important new requirements for surge protection devices, expanded ground-fault circuit interrupter coverage, and emergency disconnects for dwelling units. Shaffer Construction stays current with all code changes to ensure that every panel upgrade we complete in Inglewood meets current standards and passes inspection on the first try.

When you schedule a panel upgrade with Shaffer Construction, our electricians begin with a thorough assessment of your existing electrical system. We examine your current panel, evaluate your electrical usage patterns, discuss your future needs such as adding solar panels or an EV charger, and provide a detailed proposal with transparent pricing. Our team handles all permitting requirements with the Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety, completes the installation with minimal disruption to your daily routine, and coordinates final inspections to ensure full code compliance.

EV Charger Installation in Inglewood: Meeting 2025 Demand

Electric vehicle adoption in California continues to accelerate, with the state leading the nation in EV sales and charging infrastructure development. For Inglewood residents who have purchased or are considering an electric vehicle, installing a home charging station is no longer a luxury but a practical necessity. While public charging stations exist throughout Los Angeles, the convenience and cost savings of charging at home make residential EV charger installation one of the most requested electrical services Shaffer Construction provides.

The U.S. Department of Energy explains that California has implemented mandatory EV charger building standards requiring new single-family homes with attached garages to include electrical conduit capable of supporting a Level 2 EV charger. For existing homes in Inglewood, professional installation by a licensed C-10 electrician is required to ensure safety and code compliance. Shaffer Construction holds all necessary licenses and certifications to install EV charging equipment for both residential and commercial properties throughout Los Angeles.

As we discussed in our guide to EV charging infrastructure for Los Angeles property owners, the installation process involves several critical steps. First, our electricians perform a load calculation to determine whether your existing electrical panel has sufficient capacity to support an EV charger, which typically requires a dedicated 40-amp or 50-amp circuit for Level 2 charging. If your panel lacks capacity, we can upgrade it as part of the installation project. Next, we help you select the appropriate charging equipment based on your vehicle's requirements and charging speed preferences.

The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power offers substantial financial incentives for EV charger installation. LADWP provides rebates of up to $1,000 for Level 2 EV chargers, plus an additional $250 rebate for installing a dedicated EV charging meter. Other utility providers serving Inglewood, such as Glendale Water and Power, offer even more generous incentives, including up to $1,399 in total rebates covering both the charger and necessary panel upgrades. Shaffer Construction works directly with these utility programs to help our customers maximize available rebates and reduce their out-of-pocket installation costs.

Our residential EV charger installation services include complete project management from start to finish. We handle the permit application through the streamlined online system offered by LADWP and the Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety, install the charging equipment and any necessary electrical upgrades, coordinate required inspections, and provide instruction on operating your new charging station. For commercial properties, Shaffer Construction designs and installs multi-port charging stations that can serve multiple vehicles simultaneously, helping Inglewood businesses attract EV-driving customers and employees.

Electrical Safety Inspections and Code Compliance in Inglewood

Electrical safety should never be taken for granted. Every year, electrical failures cause thousands of house fires across the United States, resulting in billions of dollars in property damage and tragic loss of life. Many of these fires could be prevented through regular electrical safety inspections and prompt repairs of identified hazards. Shaffer Construction provides comprehensive electrical safety inspections for Inglewood homeowners and business owners who want peace of mind that their electrical systems are operating safely and in compliance with current codes.

The NEC 2023 edition includes several significant updates aimed at improving electrical safety in both residential and commercial buildings. One of the most important changes is the expansion of ground-fault circuit interrupter requirements. GFCI protection, which prevents dangerous electrical shocks by immediately shutting off power when a ground fault is detected, is now required for all plug-in appliances in areas with sinks and food preparation capabilities. This means that break rooms, kitchenettes, and similar spaces that previously did not require GFCI protection now must have it installed. Additionally, GFCI protection has been expanded to include wall-mounted ovens, counter-mounted cooking units, clothes dryers, and microwave ovens.

Arc-fault circuit interrupters represent another critical safety technology that has been expanded in the 2023 code. AFCIs detect dangerous arcing conditions that can occur when electrical wiring is damaged, improperly installed, or degraded due to age. These devices prevent electrical fires by shutting off power before a fire can start. The updated code requires AFCI protection in additional areas of the home, including sleeping quarters in fire stations, police stations, and similar facilities. For older homes in Inglewood that were built before AFCI requirements were implemented, Shaffer Construction can retrofit your electrical panel with these life-saving devices.

Surge protection is another area where the NEC 2023 has introduced new requirements. Electrical surges, whether caused by lightning strikes, utility switching, or issues with large appliances, can damage sensitive electronics and shorten the lifespan of household appliances. The updated code now requires surge protection devices to be installed in various residential and commercial settings, including single-family homes, dormitory units, hotel rooms, and nursing homes. These devices must have a minimum nominal discharge current rating of 10kA to provide adequate protection.

For property owners in Inglewood who are unsure about the condition of their electrical systems, Shaffer Construction offers detailed electrical safety inspections that examine every aspect of your system. Our licensed electricians check your electrical panel for signs of overheating, corrosion, or damage, test GFCI and AFCI devices to ensure they are functioning properly, inspect visible wiring for deterioration or improper installation, verify that all circuits are properly grounded, and identify any code violations that could pose safety risks or complicate future property sales. Following the inspection, we provide a detailed report with photographs documenting any issues found and recommendations for repairs or upgrades prioritized by urgency.

Why Professional Electrical Installation Matters in Los Angeles

California maintains some of the strictest electrical licensing requirements in the nation, and for good reason. Electrical work performed by unqualified individuals poses serious risks of fire, electrocution, and property damage. Throughout Los Angeles, including Inglewood, all electrical work must be performed by or under the supervision of a licensed C-10 electrician. This licensing requirement ensures that the person working on your electrical system has completed extensive training, passed rigorous examinations, and carries appropriate insurance to protect property owners.

Beyond licensing, proper electrical work requires obtaining permits from local building departments. Many homeowners are tempted to skip the permitting process to save money or avoid inspections, but this decision can have serious consequences. Unpermitted electrical work can void homeowner's insurance policies, create liability issues if someone is injured, make it difficult to sell your property in the future, and result in fines from building departments. The permitting process exists to ensure that electrical work is inspected by qualified inspectors who verify code compliance and safety.

Shaffer Construction handles all aspects of permitting for our Inglewood customers. Los Angeles has streamlined the permitting process for EV charger installations and many other electrical projects through online portals that provide instant approval for qualifying projects. Our familiarity with these systems allows us to obtain permits quickly and efficiently, minimizing delays and ensuring your project stays on schedule. We coordinate all required inspections, including rough-in inspections before walls are closed up and final inspections once work is complete.

The quality of electrical work also matters tremendously for long-term reliability and safety. Our electricians use only high-quality materials from reputable manufacturers, follow best practices for wire routing and connection methods, label all circuits clearly for future reference, and ensure that all work is neat and professional in appearance. These details make a significant difference in how your electrical system performs over its lifespan and how easy it will be for future electricians to work on your system if additions or repairs are needed.

For complex projects such as whole-house rewiring, service upgrades, or commercial electrical installations, Shaffer Construction provides detailed proposals that outline the scope of work, timeline, and costs before any work begins. We believe in transparent communication and never surprise our customers with unexpected charges. Our team works efficiently to minimize disruption to your home or business, cleans up thoroughly each day, and keeps you informed of progress throughout the project.
